notices.title: Thailand cut visa-free stays on Sep 15, 2026
notices.body: Most visa-free stays dropped from 60 to 30 days, and 21 nationalities now need an e-visa. Visa-free entry is for tourism only, so remote work or business needs a proper visa such as the DTV. One 30-day extension may be granted at an immigration office at the officer's discretion.

notices.title: China's visa-free trial runs through Dec 31, 2026
notices.body: Many passports (including the UK and Canada since Feb 17, 2026) can visit China visa-free for up to 30 days under a trial policy that is currently set to end Dec 31, 2026. Check before booking travel for 2027.

visas.summary: Many nationalities can visit visa-free for up to 90 days in any 180. US citizens can currently stay up to 1 year visa-free. Longer stays use the Unique Permit, which combines residence and work.

categories.name: Unique Permit: Digital nomad
categories.forWho: Remote workers employed by or contracting for companies outside Albania.
categories.processing: Often several weeks. Confirm current times on e-Albania.
documents: Work contract or client agreements from abroad

categories.name: Unique Permit: Employment or self-employment
categories.forWho: People hired locally or running their own business in Albania.

categories.name: Residence: Pensioner
categories.forWho: Retirees with a pension from abroad.

categories.name: Residence: Property owner
categories.forWho: People who own real estate in Albania.

generalDocuments: Valid passport (check the minimum validity rule)
Criminal record check (often needs an apostille)

officialLinks.label: Ministry for Europe and Foreign Affairs: visa regime
US Embassy Albania: entering and residing

visas.summary: Schengen country. Non-EU visitors get up to 90 days in any 180. For longer stays you apply for a national visa at the Spanish consulate for where you live.

categories.name: Digital nomad (telework) visa
categories.forWho: Remote workers for companies outside Spain, with a degree or 3+ years of experience.
categories.processing: Consulates cite a 10-day legal decision term, which can be extended if they ask for more documents.
documents: Degree or proof of 3+ years experience
Income of at least 200% of the Spanish minimum wage

categories.name: Non-lucrative residence visa
categories.forWho: People living off savings or passive income who will not work in Spain.
documents: Proof of sufficient passive income or savings

categories.name: Work visa
categories.forWho: People with a job offer from a Spanish employer.
categories.processing: Employer gets authorization first, then you apply at the consulate.

categories.name: Student visa
categories.forWho: People enrolled in a recognized course in Spain.

generalDocuments: Valid passport (check the minimum validity rule)
Criminal record check (often needs an apostille)

officialLinks.label: Ministry of Foreign Affairs (find your consulate)
Example: Digital nomad visa (Consulate in London)

visas.summary: Schengen country. For long stays you get a national (D) visa at a consulate, then finish your residence permit with AIMA in Portugal.

categories.name: D7: Passive income visa
categories.forWho: Retirees and people with steady passive income.
categories.processing: Legal decision target is about 60 days from a complete application. Real timelines often run longer.

categories.name: D8: Digital nomad visa
categories.forWho: Remote workers earning from outside Portugal.
categories.processing: About 60 days legal target, often longer in practice.
documents: Proof of income for the last months

categories.name: D1: Work visa
categories.forWho: People with a job contract in Portugal.

categories.name: D4: Study visa
categories.forWho: Students accepted by a Portuguese institution.

generalDocuments: Valid passport (check the minimum validity rule)
Criminal record check (often needs an apostille)

visas.summary: Visitors from many countries can enter without a visa, and the officer decides how many days you get (up to 180). To live there, you apply for residence at a Mexican consulate abroad, then finish the process with INM in Mexico.

categories.name: Temporary resident (economic solvency)
categories.forWho: People who can show income or savings above the consulate threshold. First card is usually 1 year, renewable up to 4 years total.
categories.processing: Consulates cite 1 to 10 business days from the appointment. You then have 30 days after entry to finish at INM.
documents: Bank statements (usually 6 or 12 months) or proof of income

categories.name: Temporary resident (family unity)
categories.forWho: Family of Mexican citizens or residents.

categories.name: Permanent resident
categories.forWho: Retirees with higher pension income, or people with close family ties.

visas.summary: Most visitors need either an eTA or a visitor visa. Living in Canada long term usually means a work or study permit, or permanent residence through Express Entry or a provincial program.

categories.name: Visitor (eTA or visitor visa)
categories.forWho: Short visits, usually up to 6 months.
categories.processing: eTA is often fast. Visitor visa times vary by country.

categories.name: Work permit
categories.forWho: People with a job offer or an eligible open work permit.
categories.processing: Varies a lot. Use the official processing time tool.

categories.name: Study permit
categories.forWho: Students accepted at a designated learning institution.

categories.name: Express Entry (permanent residence)
categories.forWho: Skilled workers ranked by points (age, language, education, experience).
categories.processing: Use the official tool for current times.

categories.name: Provincial Nominee Program
categories.forWho: People nominated by a province or territory.

visas.summary: Schengen country. For long stays most non-EU nationals get a national visa before arriving, then a residence permit from the local foreigners office.

categories.name: Opportunity Card (Chancenkarte)
categories.forWho: Skilled workers looking for a job in Germany. Points based.
categories.processing: Several weeks, sometimes up to a few months. Valid up to 1 year.
documents: Proof of funds (blocked account or similar)

categories.name: EU Blue Card
categories.forWho: Graduates with a qualifying job offer above the salary threshold.

categories.name: Skilled worker visa
categories.forWho: People with recognized qualifications and a job offer.

categories.name: Freelance or self-employment visa
categories.forWho: Freelancers and business founders.

categories.name: Student visa
categories.forWho: Students admitted to a German university.

generalDocuments: Valid passport (check the minimum validity rule)
Criminal record check (often needs an apostille)

visas.summary: Since 15 Sep 2026 visa-free visits are 30 days for most passports (down from 60), for tourism only. Most visas are applied for online through the Thai e-Visa system. Long-stay options include the DTV for remote workers and the LTR for higher earners.

categories.name: Destination Thailand Visa (DTV)
categories.forWho: Remote workers, freelancers, and people doing Thai soft power activities like Muay Thai or cooking courses.
categories.processing: Usually a few weeks. Since 31 Aug 2026 you must apply to the Thai embassy or consulate for your country of nationality or residence, not from a neighboring country.
documents: Proof of remote work or course enrollment
Bank statement showing at least 500,000 THB

categories.name: Long-Term Resident (LTR) visa
categories.forWho: Wealthy retirees, remote workers with high income, and highly skilled professionals.
categories.processing: Varies. Applications go through the Board of Investment.

categories.name: Non-immigrant O (retirement)
categories.forWho: Retirees aged 50+ meeting the financial requirement.

categories.name: Education (ED) visa
categories.forWho: Students enrolled at a recognized school.

generalDocuments: Proof of stay or ties to Thailand

schengen.note: Since Apr 10, 2026 the EU Entry/Exit System (EES) takes fingerprints and a photo at the border. ETIAS (the online travel authorization) is not running yet and has no confirmed start date; the EU will announce it months ahead.
